Belarusian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • moj — Łacinka (Belarusian Latin alphabet)

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *mojь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [moj]

Pronoun

[edit]

мой • (moj)

  1. (possessive) my, mine

Bulgarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *mojь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [mɔj]

Pronoun

[edit]

мой • (moj)

  1. my, mine (first-person singular possessive determiner/pronoun)
    Мо́ето и́ме е Пе́тър.
    Móeto íme e Pétǎr.
    My name is Peter.
    Та́зи кола́ не е мо́я.
    Tázi kolá ne e mója.
    That car is not mine.
    Мо́ят е о́нзи ей там, в кра́йно дя́сно.
    Mójat e ónzi ej tam, v krájno djásno.
    Mine is the one over there, on the far right.
    еди́н мой прия́тел
    edín moj prijátel
    a friend of mine
    (literally, “one my friend”)
    еди́н от мо́ите прия́тели
    edín ot móite prijáteli
    one of my friends

Komi-Permyak

[edit]
 мой on Komi-Permyak Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Permic *moj, from Proto-Uralic *maja. Cognates include Finnish majava and Erzya мияв (mijav).

Permic cognates include Komi-Zyrian мой (moj) and Udmurt мый (myj).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmoj/, [ˈmo̞j]
  • Rhymes: -oj
  • Hyphenation: мой

Noun

[edit]

мой • (moj)

  1. beaver

Ossetian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

мой • (moj)

  1. husband

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak moj, from Proto-Slavic *mojь. For sense of "husband", compare dialectal Polish mój.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmɔj]
  • Rhymes: -ɔj
  • Hyphenation: мой

Pronoun

[edit]

мой (moj)

  1. my: possessive pronoun of я (ja)

Declension

[edit]

vocative мой (moj) моя (moja) мойо (mojo) мойо (mojo)

Noun

[edit]

мой (moj) m pers (feminine equivalent моя)

  1. (familiar) my husband
  2. (familiar, in the plural) my folks, my family
    мойо нє дома ― mojo nje doma ― my folks aren't home

Russian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [moj]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -oj

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic мои (moi), from Proto-Slavic *mojь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *majas, from Proto-Indo-European *móyos (“my; mine”). Cognate with Old Prussian mais.

Pronoun

[edit]

мой • (moj)

  1. (possessive) my, mine
    «Моя́ Москва́» ― «Mojá Moskvá» ― "My Moscow"
